body:
@jrouwe The two separate stages mentioned here:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ee713ccb7cbaddf59f8258ed6663461779d00856/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_contact_listener_3d.cpp#L199-L203

... are they executed on the same job or different jobs?

I'm realizing that since we're not tracking manifolds globally anymore this check likely becomes flaky if these two stages are on different jobs, since `WorkerThreadPool` can put them on different threads.
The stages are in different jobs so it is quite likely that you get a callback on different threads: 1 = discrete callback, 2 = ccd callback.

> The stages are in different jobs so it is quite likely that you get a callback on different threads

How big of a problem would you say it is to just discard all but the first manifold for a given shape pair, like what I'm doing currently in `_flush_contacts`? The passed on manifold will randomly be either the discrete or the CCD one, so can end up flip-flopping a lot.

If it does sound like a problem, is there any way we can distinguish between the two stages that doesn't involve keeping track of already encountered shape pairs across all threads? I was hoping to not have to keep that manifold lock, even if the critical section was quite small.

> How big of a problem would you say it is to just discard all but the first manifold for a given shape pair

I think that really depends on the user of those contact points. From the looks of it, they can be requested from GDScript, so it's probably best to return consistent results.

> is there any way we can distinguish between the two stages that doesn't involve keeping track of already encountered shape pairs across all threads

No, but I can think of 2 possible ways:
1. Use the one with deepest penetration. This is almost certainly the one from the discrete step. And otherwise it will at least be deterministic.
2. Use an atomic counter that increments with every contact callback and tag the manifolds with the counter so you can pick the earlier one.

> From the looks of it, they can be requested from GDScript

Correct.

> Use an atomic counter that increments with every contact callback and tag the manifolds with the counter so you can pick the earlier one.

While this sounds like the more promising alternative, I've recently been burned by the ill effects that atomics can have on performance when written to from many threads concurrently[^1], so I would be hesitant to go down this route without doing some serious profiling first.

In either case, I would need to make `_flush_contacts` a two-phase thing if I want pick the best manifold for each shape pair before I go through with actually passing them onto `JoltBody3D`. The question then becomes whether all that extra work in `_flush_contacts` ends up costing us more than whatever contention we'd have from the lock in `_try_add_contacts`.

I'll go with the deepest penetration option for now, and do some profiling later.

[^1]: There was a great talk about it [here](https://youtu.be/tND-wBBZ8RY?t=673), if you're curious. A readers-writers lock was where I ran into this myself as well.

Alright, I think this is about as ready as it'll get.

It's been rebased, but also reworked a bit, as the soft body area stuff I had before turned out to be broken and would leak overlaps. You'll find a new `_flush_area_soft_body_events` that's somewhat similar to `_flush_area_enters`/`_flush_area_exits` (now combined into `_flush_area_body_events`) in that it "converges" the thread-local data into the actual events that get sent to `JoltArea3D`.

This prompted a few other changes as well, like `ThreadLocals::instances` now being a `SelfList` instead of a `TightLocalVector`. Not strictly necessary, but seemed like a better fit, and avoids any allocations, whatever that's worth. I definitely need to put up a PR to add range-for support for `SelfList` though.

Just to pre-emptively highlight a few things here, since they might come up during review anyway:

1. There's a number of places in this new code that assumes that a shape pair only ever gets one `JPH::ContactListener` callback per step, with sensors specifically. Does that seem like a fragile assumption, @jrouwe? Could you see that changing at some point, like if Jolt were to get CCD support for sensors or something?
2. Unlike what's currently in `master`, contacts are now reallocated every single step, because of `manifolds.clear()` in `_flush_contacts`. I have however refactored them to be more akin to Jolt's own contacts, so we now only have a single `TightLocalVector<Contact>` instead of two. I debated using a `FixedVector<Contact, 64>` instead, but I can't justify the waste, especially since contact reporting is opt-in.
3. `deepest_manifolds` in `_flush_contacts` will persist its capacity indefinitely, same as every other collection (except the contacts). All this memory that we're persisting across steps does bother me a bit, but I'm not sure if it's really that bad in the grand scheme of things, and I'm sure the allocation churn would bother me more with these hotter collections.
4. The "duplicate area soft body overlaps" error in `_flush_area_soft_body_events` is a lazy best-effort thing. It should hopefully never happen in the first place, and if it does then it won't catch everything, but that's fine.
5. I have not incorporated the optimization mentioned [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118047#issuecomment-4192676780), meant to save on `area_overlaps` checks. I suggest we try that in a separate PR instead.

Looks good to me (verified that it indeed fixes the performance issues in #118047).

> There's a number of places in this new code that assumes that a shape pair only ever gets one JPH::ContactListener callback per step, with sensors specifically. Does that seem like a fragile assumption, @jrouwe? Could you see that changing at some point, like if Jolt were to get CCD support for sensors or something?

For normal CCD bodies, it is possible to receive a 2nd `OnContactPersisted` callback. This is done from here:

https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/blob/1e19ff51a16f1452f6e85c7cfdd216b1b2efae38/Jolt/Physics/Constraints/ContactConstraintManager.cpp#L1452-L1454

This should be very rare as it means that a CCD body overlaps with an object and then somehow, after the regular velocity solve, retains enough velocity in the direction of the overlapping body to trigger CCD. This can probably only happen if the object is being pushed by another high velocity object at the same time.

For sensors, it is unlikely that I need this. The reason why that callback is called a second time is that I need to give the application a chance to override friction, restitution etc. For sensors that's not needed since they don't have a collision response.
